newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Conventional arms framework pact said to be close.
newsitem.headline: Conventional arms framework pact said to be close.

text.p: Russia and 29 other countries are close to concluding a framework agreement on amending a conventional arms treaty vital to European security, according to diplomatic sources.

Western diplomats in Moscow and Vienna, where the talks on the 1990 Conventional Force in Europe (CFE) treaty are taking place, report progress at the negotiations and say this stage of talks could be wrapped up this week.

"The idea is to get on paper the points on which there is agreement and the points which remain to be agreed. This stage of talks could be concluded in a couple of days," a Moscow-based diplomat said.
"This would be a very significant step towards a final agreement on modernisation of the treaty."
A final CFE agreement is not expected to be completed until next year, but Western diplomats in Vienna also sound positive.

"A lot of progress has been made. We are confident that we will have an agreement in the next couple of days," one said. "My impression is that the Russians also think we can come to closure (of the talks) this week."
Russian officials declined to comment on the talks, saying only that a top foreign ministry expert on CFE was expected to return from Vienna by the end of this month.
